subject: Live chat buffering & high tail-latency — recovery steps and credit offer
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@kestrelai.com>
To: support@redwoodai.com
Cc: 
Date: 2028-06-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Live chat streams intermittently buffering and long tail latency (region: us-east)

Hi team,

We saw a spike in buffering and multi-second stalls on streaming chat responses across multiple sessions starting ~09:05 UTC this morning. Our customers are seeing long tail tokens (sometimes 4–8s per token) and sessions intermittently drop the stream entirely. Sample request IDs: rq_8a3f2, rq_8a3f9, rq_8b02b.

We already tried a client retry (exponential backoff) which helped some sessions but not all; traffic is mostly below our usual volume. Can you confirm if anything on Redwood's side is affecting streaming throughput? Any short-term mitigations we can do?

Liam
Head of Platform — Kestrel AI

[Attachment: client-sample-ids.txt (text)]

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@kestrelai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T09:30:18Z
Subject: Re: Live chat streams intermittently buffering and long tail latency (region: us-east)

Hi Liam — thanks for the quick heads-up and the sample IDs. We're investigating now and have opened an incident ticket (SUP-1829).

Immediate items we've pushed live from our side to reduce impact:
- Enabled more aggressive prefix/KV caching on the affected routing cluster (us-east-1) to reduce repeated compute on common prefixes.
- Temporarily reduced per-session max_concurrency to 2 on your tenant to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Applied a soft cap on per-token CPU scheduling to prioritize active streams over background batch jobs.

Client-side mitigations we recommend (low-friction, no deploy):
1) If you can, enable client-side aggregation of partial deltas (buffer for up to 200ms before rendering) — this reduces the number of small bursts.
2) Add retry/backoff for stream reconnects with jitter (you already have this, but consider reducing initial backoff to 150ms for user-visible flows).
3) Lower the requested max_tokens for interactive prompts where acceptable (we can help identify heaviest callers).

I'll loop engineering (Ben and Marissa) for a deeper triage; we should have a short incident update in ~60 minutes.

—Olga
Enterprise Account Lead | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: incident-timeline.csv (text/csv) — initial stub]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2028-06-15T09:45:02Z
Subject: Re: Live chat streams intermittently buffering and long tail latency (region: us-east)

Heads-up — early telemetry shows a spike in kernel-level scheduling latency on a subset of inference hosts in the us-east-1 pool servicing interactive variants. Spikes align with small-token bursts (many short requests), which exposes an inefficiency in the runtime's IO loop under high small-batch concurrency.

Short-term actions I'm taking now:
- Rolling a config change to prioritize streaming RPCs over small-batch synchronous requests on the hot hosts (will apply to ~25% of your traffic first).
- Increasing internal trace collection window for affected hosts to capture exact syscall latencies.

We'll validate whether the prioritization reduces tail by measuring 95/99th percentile token emission times. If this succeeds, we'll expand the policy.

Ben
Principal SRE — Serving Runtime
[Attachment: redline-config-snippet.txt (text)]

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@kestrelai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T11:10:04Z
Subject: Re: Live chat streams intermittently buffering and long tail latency (region: us-east)

Liam — quick update: after the prioritization rollout we see 80% reduction in 99th-percentile per-token latency for affected hosts. Some customer sessions still experienced a small number of stalls while the rollout completed. Full mitigation for your tenant achieved at 10:48 UTC.

What we changed that mattered:
- RPC prioritization policy (streaming > short-batch) on hot path.
- More aggressive prefix cache warming for frequent prompt fingerprints.

Next steps / follow-ups we will do (ETA timeline):
- Today (EOD): collect and share a short CSV of affected request IDs and timestamps (we will match to your sample IDs) — attachment in this thread.
- 48 hours: deploy a micro-optimization to runtime IO loop (non-disruptive A/B) to reduce syscall overhead for small token emits.
- 7 days: postmortem and proposed preventative work (kernel scheduling mitigations / scheduler fallback).

As a gesture for the customer impact, I can offer a one-time credit against your June usage; details in the postmortem. Are you OK for us to proceed with a 10% credit for the 09:00–11:00 UTC window while we finalize the write-up?

Olga
[On Fri, Jun 15, 2028 at 09:12, Liam O'Connor <liam@kestrelai.com> wrote:
> We saw a spike in buffering and multi-second stalls on streaming chat responses...
> ]

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@kestrelai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-18T16:47:00Z
Subject: Post-incident summary: Kestrel AI streaming buffering (2028-06-15) — actions and credits

Hi Liam,

Attached is a concise post-incident summary covering: timeline, root cause hypothesis, short-term mitigations we applied, proposed engineering fixes, and the credit we applied to your account. Key points:

- Incident window: 2028-06-15 09:05–10:48 UTC (full mitigation applied at 10:48).
- Root cause (summary): scheduler and runtime IO contention on a subset of us-east hosts that preferentially affected small-token streaming workloads; workload pattern (high frequency of short requests) exposed an inefficiency in our IO loop leading to syscall latency spikes.
- Remediation completed: prioritization policy & KV-cache warming; these eliminated the observable tail for your traffic.
- Next engineering work: micro-optimizations to the IO loop (A/B trial next 48h), and a change to autoscaling heuristics to avoid mixed small-batch/stream contention on the same hosts (targeted in our July sprint).

Credit: we applied a 10% service credit against your billed usage for the incident window (ref KST-4521-CREDIT-1). That credit should be visible on your billing page within 24 hours.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf (full write-up), incident-timeline.csv (matched request IDs), redline-config-snippet.txt (config we applied).

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical walk-through with Ben and Marissa to go over telemetry and the planned fixes — available slots: Mon/Tue next week.

Thanks again for flagging this quickly and for working through mitigations with us. If there are any questions or additional billing needs for this window, let me know.

—Olga
Enterprise Account Lead | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: postmortem-draft.pdf (application/pdf)]
